glossary.term: A very important rule about applying these scales
glossary.definition: If, after finding your level on any scale, you do not feel better than you when you started trying to ascertain that level, you have chosen a wrong level. When you correctly find a level, you will gener feel better, i.e., brighter, more cheerful, less depressed, smarter, less confused, less concerned, less worried, and so forth. Often, will have a realization, as in: "Oh, so that's why..." For example, if you are actually at Level II, and you decide you are at some other level, say Level I or Level III, you will ei feel worse or the same. If you are actually at Level II, designating yourself Level II will perk you up, or calm you down, as the may be. People often err in the direction of selecting too high a level, so, if the results are not good, look south. Often a person has chosen a harmonic of the correct level. That is, he is actually at a higher or, more commonly, lower le which is similar to the correct level. This is most common when working with spiral scales because Levels I and VIl appear to similar or congruent, or when working with scales of alternating directions (inflow / outflow), in which case the correct leve usually flowing in the same direction as the one you have wrongly chosen.

if you feel worse after selecting a level, you have probably selected the wrong level. If the situation worsens a selecting a level, you have probably selected the wrong level. If you cannot figure out how to get up to the next higher level, or ! it impossible to do so, you have probably selected the wrong level. When you find the correct level, you will generally feel be you will usually be able to figure out how to move up a level (if it is possible to do so), and you will eventually move up to the r higher level, if you persist. Again, there are a few scales which you may not be able to ascend easily or swiftly, but you will still and do, better just knowing what level you are at, if you spot it correctly. How can one use these scales to help others? The best way to introduce someone to this subject is to use a specific scale to help him or her resolve a specific problem. Th done as follows: 1) Get the person to explain his or her situation as fully as possible. Select the appropriate scale(s) for the situation. If you have studied the scales well, this should be easy, as it is o Have him or her study the entire scale carefully, being certain the reader knows the correct definition of each word. W (s)he is done studying the scale, ask if (s)he has any questions about it, or disagreements with it. If so, clear these usually by clarifying the meanings of relevant words. Help him or her find where (s)he is on the scale. This step alone should bring considerable relief. If it does not, probably have the wrong level, or, less likely, the wrong scale. Time spent on this step is a wise investment. You might "How are you manifesting this level?" Often, this is all one need do, as one will usually have a realization about his or situation, as a result of this step.

levels.description: Saint fits when your purpose is organized around service, truth, courage, and a concern larger than ordinary self-interest. In real life, this can feel like acting from conscience even when there is no personal reward or audience. Choose this only if the motive is not status, winning, safety, or image, but a steady orientation toward the highest good you can perceive.

levels.description: Telepathy fits when influence happens through clear intention, presence, or will before much explanation is needed. People may respond because the signal is coherent, not because you are performing persuasion. Choose this when influence feels nearly direct and effortless, rather than charismatic, logical, forceful, or guilt-based.

levels.label: NO CHOICE (NECESSARY) (Transcendence)
levels.description: No necessary choice fits when you are outside the pressure of the decision. The area is so integrated or transcended that choosing is unnecessary for you to remain whole. Choose this when freedom comes from not needing the outcome, not from avoiding the decision.
